meta.title: Find running stacks and routes in the browser: proposed

frontend.label: UI step where the work started

nodes.label: Follow All Stacks link
nodes.explanation: Every surface that knows about stacks leads to the directory, because devhost never opens a browser: All Stacks on devbox sits in the toolbar's stack name menu with its other toolbar items, and the plain-HTTP 404, stack-run-stop's stopped-stack page and the status pages carry the same link; devhost start prints 'All stacks on devbox: https://devhost.localhost/' after its ready line, and devhost stack list and devhost stack info (devhost status) print it too (stack-run-stop's slice). Links use the directory's current address from the applied shared Caddy settings, under the remote or relay suffix on a page opened through it, and open in the same tab (SURF-15, MENU-1, MENU-2, WORD-2, O61, O62). While the local certificate authority is untrusted, first-run-setup's trust line leads the page (first-run-setup-02, owned by first-run-setup). Resolves stack-directory-06's slice: the toolbar and the 404 link to the directory.

nodes.label: Stacks on devbox
nodes.explanation: GET / on the directory hostname opens the page: the heading 'Stacks on devbox', the totals '3 stacks · 1 serve session · 1 failed · 1 with an agent waiting for you · 2 stopped recently' and a title such as '(2) 1 failed · 1 waiting · Stacks on devbox' (ACT-6, ACT-7, WORD-5, O16, O61). Cards sit in one column in 'Needs you', 'Running' and 'Stopped recently'; within a group stacks sort by name, then the main worktree first, so two worktrees of one project sit together and read apart: 'Acme Shop · main ~/acme', 'Acme Shop · fix-nav ~/acme/.worktrees/fix-nav' (SEL-4, SEL-6, WORD-11). Serve sessions use serve-folder's folder, port and command cards (WORD-1, serve-command-06). One line says the page is read-only and updates every 2 s (MENU-3, MENU-6, O10). Empty: 'No stacks are running on devbox. Start one with devhost start in its folder.' (STATE-2). Keys: the document's own (KEY-1, KEY-10). Resolves stack-directory-03, serve-command-06's slice and the totals of stack-directory-02.

sources.label: Replaces: totals of stacks and URLs only
Replaces: name, path, the supervisor's PID

nodes.label: Who may read it
nodes.explanation: From another environment the directory opens on its hostname under the remote or relay suffix, which the relay forwards (agent-chat's work under O36, O47, O55). Every request goes through O36's check, agent-chat's classifier: this machine and browsers signed in with the devhost passkey or paired read the page and press Check Again; a reader that stackDirectoryAllowRemote alone admits reads it without signing in, with Check Again unavailable and waiting agents counted only; any other client gets 403 with 'Sign in with passkey or pair this browser to use devhost here' and Sign In with Passkey. A relay visitor never counts as this machine; on the directory's hostname under the local suffix, this machine's browser counts as this machine, as on a stack's hostname (O36). The directory hostname also serves agent-chat's passkey routes and cookie hop. While no stack answers, Caddy cannot check a session, so its static page answers this machine, or everyone with the setting on (HOLD-7, HOLD-8, O36, O47; Backend 11).

Replaces: Caddy refuses every remote client
Replaces: relay forwards leased hosts only

nodes.label: Filter as you type
nodes.explanation: The field 'Filter stacks and services' narrows the cards as the person types, with no form and no reload; it matches stack name, worktree label, service names, hostnames and a serve session's folder, address, name and command, never a manifest file's or the devhost config file's path (SEL-10, KEY-9). Another stack keeps only its matching rows with '5 more services hidden by the filter'; the match is highlighted and group headers count what they show (SEL-10, BAR-3, WORD-5). No match reads 'No stack or service matches "serch"' with Clear Filter (STATE-2); a hostname that matches nothing offers up to three close running hostnames with the path kept, O46's rule, which is where a mistype that failed over HTTPS recovers (O46, O63, CC-27). Escape clears; Enter does nothing more. Refresh Stacks is a button of its own (FB-1, KEY-11). Resolves the filter half of stack-directory-07 and the directory half of stack-directory-04.

sources.label: Replaces: GET form; Refresh / filter button
Replaces: server filter on file paths

nodes.label: Read a stack's card
nodes.explanation: Every word on a card comes from the state the stack's services runtime publishes, the one the toolbar and devhost stack info read, drawn with services-panel's shared state indicator (ACT-2, ACT-13, SURF-14, O62). The header names the stack, its worktree label and its state: 'failed · 4 of 6 running · 1 exited · 1 not started' (ACT-6, SEL-4). Rows give cause and time: 'exited with code 3 at 17:15' with its last output line, 'failed its health check · since 17:14', 'blocked', 'not started · left out of this run' (FAIL-3, WORD-8). Each state's lead action is one step away: a link to the service's status page and the same terminal command with Copy, since the directory stays read-only (MENU-5, MENU-6, O10). A waiting agent links agent-chat's chat/open route (REV-9, CC-38). At 320 px each row keeps its state shape and word (ACT-13, serve-command-10). Resolves stack-directory-02, serve-command-10, with stack-directory-08 and stack-directory-09 on the rows.

sources.label: Replaces: green only for Running, gray rest

nodes.label: Configuration applied?
nodes.explanation: Manifest files · 2 expands the stack's manifest files, named by kind: 'Root manifest · devhost.toml'; one file reads 'Manifest files · 1'. Each says whether the stack runs it: 'Applied 17:03', or 'Not applied · rejected at 17:12 · line 42: expected ]' with 'the stack runs the accepted manifest' (UNDO-6, HOLD-6, MENU-4). A file that was not applied opens on 'Running version' with 'Version on disk' beside it and the rejected line marked; files show line numbers. Each file shows its path and line, 'devhost.toml:42', with Copy; devhost opens no editor (O51, SURF-15). The toggle has a 3:1 boundary and is 24 px tall (SURF-9, serve-command-10). The devhost config file is listed once, at the foot of the page (WORD-1). The label is 'Manifest files' (WORD-1). The caveat printed on every card today goes. Resolves stack-directory-05.

sources.label: Replaces: files read from disk only
Replaces: collapsible files, fixed caveat

nodes.label: Published state, live
nodes.explanation: While the page is visible it reads GET /stacks.json on the directory hostname 2 s after the previous read ended, and nothing while hidden (ACT-12). A live stack's control server answers with every stack's snapshot, each asked in parallel with a 2 s deadline over loopback, under the same rules as / (Backend 5). Each snapshot carries the published service state (CC-25): cause, since when, health and external checks, blocked repositories, changed files; no state defaults to running, and the runtime runs every health check while the directory reads (Backend 1). Updates move cards, totals and the title in place, never focus, and the announcer says once each change that starts or ends a need (FB-9, KEY-6). With no stack running, Caddy serves static stacks.json and stacks.html with the stopped-stack records (CC-27). Resolves stack-directory-09, the live half of stack-directory-07 and stack-directory-08's published blocked state.

sources.label: Reuses: one read per stack, 2 s deadline
Replaces: status words, Running default

nodes.label: Check Again
nodes.explanation: A blocked repository's condition line and a service that is not reachable offer Check Again: GET /stacks.json?check=<stack> asks that stack to run its external checks and read its worktree list now, which stops nothing and starts no operation; services-panel documents it in CC-37 beside its own check route (HOLD-1, HOLD-4, ACT-9; Backend 10). The button keeps focus while busy, 'Checking search…', and its result replaces the row's state and time (KEY-11, FB-9). Blocked services read blocked, never starting or running, under 'The saved worktree ~/acme-admin/.worktrees/old was deleted; devhost started none of its 3 services', said once with the way back on the status page. This machine and signed-in or paired browsers press it; a reader admitted only by stackDirectoryAllowRemote sees it unavailable with 'Sign in with passkey or pair this browser to check stacks from here' (O47, HOLD-7). Resolves stack-directory-08; carries stack-directory-09's external checks.

nodes.label: Mistyped hostname
nodes.explanation: A hostname that no live stack routes, mistyped or from a stale bookmark. Over HTTPS it gets no certificate, because Caddy issues them only for configured hostnames, so the browser shows its own connection error and the person recovers in the directory's filter (O63). On plain HTTP, with httpEnabled = true, it reaches Caddy's fallback site, as today. A recently stopped stack's hostname never gets here: its configured route stays for O15's 24 hours and answers the stopped-stack page.

sources.label: Reuses: fallback; tls internal, no on-demand

nodes.label: Did you mean …?
nodes.explanation: On plain HTTP a page load of an unrouted hostname gets devhost's own page with status 404, leading with what was asked for: 'No devhost route for hotfix-shpo.shop.localhost/checkout', before the status code in reading order (SURF-16, FB-9, WORD-7, O63). Its lead action is the close hostname with the path and query kept, 'Did you mean hotfix-shop.shop.localhost/checkout?', by O46's rule: a remembered stopped stack named first (its hostname reaches this page on plain HTTP, since only its HTTPS route is kept), then two edits by optimal string alignment, one for names of four characters or fewer, never a renumbered name, at most three, closest first; then All Stacks on devbox (MENU-5, SEL-10, SURF-15, O46, O61). 'Hostnames on devbox' groups every routed hostname by stack and worktree. A request that is not a page load gets a 404 under 2 KB that names the hostname and the directory, the answer startup-and-recovery's no-route state hands off (FB-11, agent-cli-journey-04). Resolves stack-directory-04 and the 404's link of stack-directory-06.

sources.label: Replaces: 404 title and Caddy wording
Replaces: active hostnames as bare links
Replaces: one page for every request

nodes.label: Service page opens
nodes.explanation: A route link opens, in the same tab, the app when its service runs, or devhost's status page for a service that is not running, which leads with that cause's action (Restart, Start, the way back to a worktree); the link says so: 'https://reports.shop.localhost/ · status page' (SURF-15, MENU-5). An agent waiting for the person opens its stack's page through agent-chat's GET /__devhost__/chat/open with docked chat on the decision card in one activation (REV-9, ACT-6, CC-38). This is the journey's outcome in place: the person reaches the page they chose. There is no Undo: the directory writes nothing, so nothing needs undoing and no rollback applies (UNDO-1); the browser's Back returns to the directory, which keeps its ?q= filter.

sources.label: Reuses: service URLs as same-tab links

nodes.label: Per-stack activity path
nodes.explanation: The directory's hostname serves /__devhost__/stacks/<stack>/agents/activity and its socket, the Watch Live Activity page running-agents draws and its agents record links, for this machine and browsers signed in with the passkey or paired; stackDirectoryAllowRemote admits no one to it, any other client gets 403 with O36's sentence, and no app hostname serves it (O55, O36, HOLD-7). <stack> is the stack's key, 'acme-shop', with six hexadecimal characters of its root manifest's path only while two stacks share a name, so it survives devhost stack restart, devhost restart and devhost upgrade; the directory site routes each key to that stack's current control server and rewrites the route when a replacing run registers (O18; Backend 13). running-agents owns the page and the record's activity.url; this flow owns the route.

sources.label: Replaces: every other path answers 404

nodes.label: Stopped recently
nodes.explanation: A stack that stopped within O15's 24 hours after a run of at least a minute keeps a card in 'Stopped recently', read from stack-run-stop's stopped-stack record, with when and why it stopped, 'stopped at 02:14 after 30 min without requests (idleTimeout)' or 'killed at 09:02; the devhost supervisor ended without cleaning up', and devhost start in its folder with Copy (ACT-10, STATE-2, STATE-3, UNDO-5, O15, CC-27). Its hostnames are links: they keep their configured HTTPS routes and answer the stopped-stack page (O63). A killed stack names each service it left running, 'Still running from its killed run: api (PID 8812, port 4000)', with devhost stop in its folder (ACT-11). An open page moves a stack that stops here within 4 s and says so once (FB-9). With nothing running, Caddy's static page lists these too. Resolves the empty state of stack-directory-07; reads the record of stack-run-stop-11 (owned by stack-run-stop).

sources.label: Replaces: static empty directory page
Replaces: empty-state copy

nodes.label: No stack answers
nodes.explanation: When no stack answers within 2 s, because the one devhost supervisor that runs every stack ended or stopped answering, Caddy answers the directory hostname itself: its error handler serves the static page devhost last wrote, with status 503, listing the stacks registered then, each drawn unknown, 'unknown · did not answer within 2 s · last seen 17:03', never stopped, with devhost start and devhost stop in its folder with Copy for a stack that ended, and once that devhost stack list shows what still runs and that devhost start starts a stack again once the supervisor has ended; no live devhost page can draw a stalled supervisor (STATE-4, STATE-3, ACT-5, FAIL-2, O16, R7-100). It retries every 2 s while visible, Refresh Stacks asks at once, and the live directory returns in place, announced once (ACT-12, FB-9, KEY-11). A request that is not a page load gets one short 503 line (FB-11). A stack record devhost cannot read is named in one condition line, with Copy Error holding the original error and its path, while every readable stack stays listed (FAIL-2, WORD-7). Resolves stack-directory-10.

sources.label: Replaces: handle_errors plain-text 503
Replaces: record error as plain 503
Replaces: one bad record fails the list

nodes.label: A stack does not answer
nodes.explanation: Every stack runs in one devhost supervisor with its own control port, and Caddy tries each port in turn. When one stack's control server stops answering while the others answer, it never holds the page: Caddy's health checks, every 2 s with a 1 s timeout, skip it within about 3 s and another stack serves the directory; a load that reached it moves on after a 4 s response timeout, longer than the 2 s per-stack wait (Backend 12 (e)). Its card keeps its last rows as unknown, 'unknown · did not answer within 2 s · last seen 17:15:02', never stopped or failed, offers cd ~/acme && devhost stack restart with Copy and Copy Error, and names no PID; the totals count it, '1 unknown' (ACT-5, STATE-3, STATE-4, WORD-6, FAIL-2, MENU-5, R7-100). Ctrl-Z in a foreground terminal suspends only that terminal, so no page says to run fg. When it answers again it reads live; a new run takes over its card with 'Acme Shop was replaced by devhost stack restart at 14:12', each announced once (ACT-12, FB-9). Resolves stack-directory-11.

sources.label: Replaces: first port, no health checks
Replaces: raw 'Stack details unavailable'

cards.title: What changes versus today
items: Removed: the combined Refresh / filter button and the form that reloaded the page through every stack; server-side filtering on file paths; Show all stacks; the URL count; the caveat on every card; the raw UTC Registered time and the folder under every row; Running as a default and one gray badge for six states; Active hostnames and Caddy's wording on the 404; the plain-text 503 and the raw record error; 'Stack details unavailable' on a silent stack's card; External, Directory and 'Manifest-free file or port session' on serve session cards

Merged: the directory's status words and the toolbar's become one published state drawn by one shared indicator, in the words devhost stack info prints; Clear filter and Show all stacks become Clear Filter; an HTTPS typo recovers in the filter

New: worktree labels; Needs you, Running and Stopped recently; the title's attention prefix; updates every 2 s; filtering as you type with close hostnames; Refresh Stacks; causes and times on rows; lead actions as links and commands with Copy; Check Again; waiting agents as links; applied or not applied with both versions; the plain-HTTP 404's asked-for hostname and close match with the path kept; the 503 page listing the stacks devhost last knew; short answers for requests that are not page loads; health checks that hand the page to another stack; O36's check with a sign-in page; each stack's Watch Live Activity path; serve-folder's serve session cards

Changed: statuses update while the page is open and stopped stacks stay listed for 24 hours (CC-27); the filter keeps only matching rows; one unreadable stack record no longer hides the other stacks; a stack that stops answering no longer holds the page; cards are keyed by stack ID and show no PID; signed-in or paired browsers read the directory and press Check Again (O47)

Kept: one page for every stack on the machine, any live stack serving it with a 2 s deadline per stack; this machine by default, stackDirectoryAllowRemote still meaning anyone may read it, GET and HEAD only, loopback snapshots, no-store and no-referrer; the reserved hostname; configured-hosts-only TLS; read-only, no writes, no browser or editor opened; same-tab links; ?q= links; devhost start still refuses while a stack record cannot be read

cards.title: Backend work
items: The snapshot reads the published service state (services-panel's); no state is a default; health, daemon and external checks run while the directory reads
Stack fields: state and summary, worktree labels, foreground or detached, start time, last outcome, blocked reasons, the stack's key, serve-folder's sessionKind and command
Waiting agents with agent-chat's chat/open link, counted only for readers O36 does not admit
Configuration state: applied or not applied, the structured rejection, the accepted text while it differs
GET /stacks.json beside /; static stacks.json and stacks.html with stopped-stack records and the registered stacks
The filter moves to the page with the shared close-hostname matcher; order by need, then name, main worktree first
The plain-HTTP 404 embeds routes by stack and worktree; a short 404 for requests that are not page loads
The directory's URL and machine name for the toolbar and the status pages
Check Again: GET /stacks.json?check=<stack>, for this machine and signed-in or paired browsers
O36's check in the directory guard; the static page refuses relayed and remote clients unless stackDirectoryAllowRemote; agent-chat's passkey routes on the directory hostname
handle_errors serves the static page and data with 503, one short line otherwise; a reader that names unreadable stack records; the re-render after a dead devhost drops its control port
Health checks on the proxy hop, a response timeout longer than the 2 s per-stack wait and a retry count; a silent stack reported unknown with its stack ID, never a PID
Per-stack routes for /__devhost__/stacks/<stack>/agents/activity to each stack's current control server

cards.title: Contract changes
items: CC-27: stopped stacks stay listed with when, why and the start command; cards count running services and update while the page is open; close hostnames on the plain-HTTP 404 and in the directory (O46, O63)

Read, unchanged here: CC-25 (published service state), CC-38 (sessions across worktrees, chat/open), CC-11 (devhost service commands), CC-23 (devhost stack info), CC-37 (Check Again routes), CC-39 (machineName)
CC-50: stack-lifecycle.md's counts, Configuration, Refresh / filter, Clear filter, remote readers, serving and unavailable-page sentences, for the reference's author beside CC-27 and CC-31
